source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Electrical-Body and Chassis, p.12-32

procedures.title: Speedometer or tachometer head replacement
steps: Remove the left-hand cluster from the car first.
Unplug the odometer reset and speedminder connectors from the back of the speedometer head.
Remove the 3 screws holding the head to the back of the cluster and lift the head out carefully.
Move the wiper solenoid to the back of the new tachometer and/or the speedminder buzzer to the back of the new speedometer, then fasten the head to the cluster bezel.
Reconnect the odometer and/or speedminder reset cable at the back of the speedometer.
Reinstall the left-hand cluster.

procedures.title: Speedometer and tachometer cable replacement or lubrication
steps: Disconnect the cable at the speedometer or tachometer head and pull the old core out from the head end of the conduit.
If the core is broken, remove the lower piece from the transmission or distributor end.
Coat the lower 3/4 of the core with AC speedometer cable lubricant and feed it into the conduit.
Connect the upper end to the head and road test to confirm it works.
notes: Do not kink the cable housings.

procedures.title: Center gauges (fuel, temperature, ammeter, oil pressure): service notes
steps: Remove the center instrument panel (gauge pack) before taking out any of these gauges.
Fuel gauge: check the gas gauge fuse in the fuse panel before troubleshooting the gauge or tank sender.
Temperature gauge: test and replace faulty units; do not try to repair the engine unit or gauge.
When fitting a new engine temperature unit, use no thread compound, since it raises resistance and gives false readings.
Ammeter: keep the terminals clean and tight.
Oil pressure gauge: if the pressure line becomes restricted, blow it out or replace it.
notes: The fuel gauge circuit is the cluster gauge plus a float-controlled rheostat in the tank.

procedures.title: Clock replacement
steps: Remove the set shaft knob screw and the knob.
Remove the screws holding the clock to the back of the housing and take the clock out from the rear.
Install in reverse order.

procedures.title: Seat belt and door ajar indicators
steps: Replace the seat belt indicator (a push-reset thermal switch fed from the fuel gauge terminal) as a complete unit.
For the door ajar indicator, check the bulb and the remote door jamb switch on the lock pillar.
